name: Shadow stroke warm-up
purpose: Wake up the strokes without a ball: slow, then match speed, all wings.

variants.instructions: One minute each: forehand, backhand, push, then your main attacking stroke. Start at half speed and finish at match speed. Recover to ready after every stroke.

success.description: 4 strokes warmed up, back to ready every time.

coachingPoints: Feel the turn of the body

name: Push warm-up rally
purpose: Soft hands and touch before the main work: easy push rallies.

variants.instructions: Backhand push rally for one minute, forehand push rally for one minute, then any push anywhere.
Gentle backspin balls, alternating sides. Push each one low.
variants.feederInstructions: Light backspin, alternating sides, slow rhythm.

variants.instructions: Robot on light backspin, alternating sides. Push each ball low.

name: Forehand-backhand warm-up
purpose: Warm up both wings and the first small steps.

variants.instructions: Your partner blocks one to your forehand, one to your backhand, at an easy pace.
Easy topspin alternating forehand and backhand.
Robot oscillating at an easy pace between forehand and backhand.
Rebound board up. One forehand, one backhand, easy pace.

name: Three targets: wide forehand, wide backhand, elbow
purpose: Placement on purpose: hit the three targets that make opponents move most.

variants.instructions: Put three targets on your partner's side: wide forehand, wide backhand, middle (their elbow). Call a target before each shot and hit it.
Three targets on the far side. The feeder calls a target as each ball comes.
variants.feederInstructions: Steady topspin; call 'forehand', 'backhand' or 'elbow' as you feed.

variants.instructions: Three targets. Hit them in order: wide forehand, elbow, wide backhand. Repeat.
Three tape marks on the board: left, middle, right. Hit them in order.

coachingPoints: Aim with the body and bat angle
Wide means wide: off the side line
The elbow is the hardest place to defend

name: Change pace and spin
purpose: Mix a slow, spinny ball into fast rallies to break the opponent's rhythm.

variants.instructions: Rally: every third ball must be clearly different: slow and spinny, or flat and fast. Then play games where a point won after a change counts 2.
Robot on steady topspin. Play two fast drives, then one slow, heavy loop. Count clean sets of three.
Steady topspin feed. Fast, fast, slow-and-spinny. Repeat.
variants.feederInstructions: Steady topspin, same spot, steady rhythm.

success.description: 7 of 10 sets with a clear change.

coachingPoints: Recover after the slow one: it can come back fast

name: Playing a chopper
purpose: Patience against backspin defence: spin, the middle, and a drop shot when they're far back.

variants.instructions: Your partner chops (or pushes long from far back). Loop with spin to the middle; after 3 loops, try a drop shot. Games to 11.
Robot on heavy backspin, long, random sides. Loop with spin, not speed. Every fourth ball, step in and loop harder.
Long heavy backspin to random sides. Loop each with spin; every fourth ball, go for a winner.

coachingPoints: Spin first; speed only on the loose ball
Bring them in with a drop shot

name: Playing a blocker
purpose: Give a blocker no pace to use: slow spinny loops, then the kill.

variants.instructions: Your partner only blocks. Open with slow, heavy loops to the wide corners; kill the first high block. Games to 11.
Robot on medium topspin to random sides. Loop slow and heavy twice, then a fast one.

coachingPoints: Slow and heavy beats fast and flat here

name: Quick feet ladder
purpose: Fast, light feet with no jumping. Tape or chalk a ladder on the floor.

variants.instructions: A ladder of 8 squares (tape or imagined). Two feet in each square forward; one foot in each square forward; side steps through it. 3 rounds with 30 seconds rest.

name: Split squat jumps
purpose: Explosive legs for the first step.

variants.instructions: Lunge position, jump and switch legs in the air, land softly. 3 sets of 8 each side, 45 seconds rest.

coachingPoints: Front knee in line with the toes, not caving in

name: Walking lunges with a turn
purpose: Strong, stable legs and a mobile upper body, without jumping.

variants.instructions: Walking lunges, turning the upper body toward the front leg each step. 2 sets of 10 each leg.

coachingPoints: Back knee close to the floor

name: Shoulder and wrist care
purpose: Keep the playing arm healthy: small, slow, controlled.

variants.instructions: With a light band or bottle: 15 external rotations, 15 internal rotations, 10 slow arm raises to the side, 15 wrist flexions and extensions, 15 forearm turns. Both arms.

success.description: The full routine, slow and controlled.

coachingPoints: Both arms, not just the playing arm

name: Core rotation circuit
purpose: Link legs to arm: a strong, rotating middle.

variants.instructions: 2 rounds: 30 seconds dead bug, 30 seconds side plank each side, 12 slow standing trunk turns holding a bottle out in front, 30 seconds bird dog.

name: Handling nerves
purpose: A plan for when your heart races: notice it, breathe, simplify.

variants.instructions: Picture a close game at 9–9. Notice where you feel nervous. Do 3 slow out-breaths, pick one simple target for the next point (for example: 'serve short, attack the long push'), and say it once to yourself. Repeat 5 times.

coachingPoints: Nerves are normal; they mean it matters

name: One cue per point
purpose: Train attention: pick one cue before each point and judge only that.

variants.instructions: For 10 imaginary points: choose one cue (for example: 'watch their bat'), shadow the point, then rate yourself 1–3 only on that cue.
Play 10 points. Before each, say one cue out loud. After each, rate yourself 1–3 on that cue only, not on the score.

coachingPoints: Judge the cue, not the result

name: See it before you play it
purpose: Rehearse your best patterns in your head: it helps them happen at the table.

variants.instructions: Eyes closed, 2 minutes: picture your favourite serve and third-ball pattern 5 times, in real speed, from your own eyes. Feel the bat, hear the ball.

coachingPoints: Include the feeling of a good contact

name: Cool-down with breathing
purpose: Slow walk, stretches and a calm close to the session.

variants.instructions: One minute slow walk. Then hold each for 20–30 seconds: hip flexors, hamstrings, shoulders across the chest, forearm of the playing arm. Finish with 5 slow breaths and one thing you did well today.

success.description: Breathing calm, one good thing named.

coachingPoints: Name one thing that went well

name: Mobility warm-up
purpose: Open hips, spine and shoulders before playing.

variants.instructions: 45 seconds each: march on the spot, hip circles, world's greatest stretch (lunge + reach) each side, thoracic turns, arm swings across and back, wrist and ankle circles, then 20 seconds of quick feet.
